action: Prepare a Gas Master Plan and gas flaring policy consistent with Nigeria’s 2060 net zero targets as provided by the energy transition plan and the NDCs
comment: The Nigeria Gas Master Plan 2026 was launched by NNPC Ltd in January 2026, replacing the 2008 plan and establishing production targets of 10 bcf/d by 2027 and 12 bcf/d by 2030 alongside a $60 billion investment ambition. Implementation is governed by a dedicated Implementation Assurance Team. M300 support will focus on the gas-to-power interface, including alignment between GMP 2026 pipeline priorities and generation capacity planning under the NIRP.

commitment: Integrated least-cost power system planning adopted incorporating regional resources
action: Ministry of Power prepares the Hydro Power Master Plan
comment: The Nigeria Hydropower Development Master Plan (HMP), together with an accompanying Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment, is being developed by the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Power, and is financed under the World Bank-supported Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Programme. Expressions of interest were invited from consulting firms and closed in January 2026, with the Request for Proposals scheduled for issuance in February 2026. Preparation of the Plan is expected to take approximately 18 months from the commencement of the consultancy. Procurement remains ongoing as of September 2026.

commitment: Integrated least-cost power system planning adopted incorporating regional resources
action: Under the leadership of the Ministry of Power, Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE) and the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC) to develop a PPP framework for investment in large hydropower projects
comment: Preparatory work is embedded in the World Bank-supported SPIN Programme, which will, with IFC support, prepare at least one large hydropower project under a PPP model and address enabling-environment constraints. The broader PPP architecture has meanwhile strengthened through ICRC's revised guidelines and Model PPP Agreement, and transactions continue under existing processes; the 460MW Katsina-Ala plant reached commercial close in May 2026. Progress on this milestone depends on the Hydropower Master Plan, currently at the procurement stage, which will define the pipeline and PPP structuring approach.

On 30 June 2026, TCN handed over a control room extension at the Gwagwalada 330kV substation to NISO as an interim National Control Centre, pending completion of the permanent facility. NISO is also targeting substantial completion of related grid-monitoring infrastructure, including IoT meter installations across the remaining transmission-distribution interfaces by Q4 2026, aiming for full generation-to-distribution grid visibility by year-end.

commitment: Adopt and enforce harmonized transmission pricing within the respective power pools to facilitate the power trade across borders
action: Adoption of a Transmission Charging Model
comment: The regulatory foundation for non-TCN participation at the transmission level has been established through the Order on Registration and Authorisation of Grid-Connected Private Transmission Substations (NERC/2026/013), effective March 2026, which creates an Independent Electricity Transmission Network Operator permit for bulk consumers connecting to the 132kV and 330kV networks. The Order does not, however, establish a commercial framework for private investment in shared transmission infrastructure; no transmission tariff, competitive tendering mechanism or availability-based remuneration structure currently exists for independent transmission projects. M300 support will therefore focus on developing that framework, drawing on comparative experience from Kenya, Brazil and India.

The Order does not, however, establish a commercial framework for private investment in shared transmission infrastructure; no transmission tariff, competitive tendering mechanism or availability-based remuneration structure currently exists for independent transmission projects. commitment: Adopt and enforce harmonized transmission pricing within the respective power pools to facilitate the power trade across borders
action: Synchronization of West African Grids
comment: Following the November 2025 synchronisation test, WAPP continued its regional integration efforts: NISO was formally admitted into WAPP in January 2026, and by July 2026 the grids of Nigeria, Ghana, Benin and Togo had been successfully synchronised. WAPP also advanced the 1,550-km Nigeria–Benin–Togo–Ghana–Côte d'Ivoire transmission corridor that same month, a step toward establishing a unified regional electricity market. On infrastructure, the Côte d'Ivoire–Liberia–Sierra Leone–Guinea interconnector is now operational, with Côte d'Ivoire already exporting power to Guinea and Sierra Leone. The North Core Project, only 56% complete at the end of 2025, may face further delays beyond 2026 due to security and logistical challenges.                                                                                                While partial synchronisation has advanced faster than expected, full regional integration remains contingent on completion of the North Core Project, which, after multiple delays (2023→2024→2025), has no confirmed new completion date as of mid-2026, with security and logistical constraints cited as the primary risk of further slippage.WAPP has not committed to a new completion date.

NERC also granted a derogation raising the ceiling for DARES-eligible projects to 10MW, accommodating the programme's 42 interconnected sites (0.9–10MW, averaging 5.879MW).

action: Establish/scale-up results-based financing (RBF) facility for distributed renewable energy
comment: Completed. Results-based financing for distributed renewable energy is established and operating at scale under DARES, comprising a $300 million stand-alone solar RBF component with independent verification, and a Performance-Based Grant programme for isolated mini-grids. The facility has been scaled through commercial co-financing, including ₦100 billion facilities from Lotus Bank and FCMB and a $188 million solar financing platform launched in May 2026, with disbursements to developers ongoing.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: Periodic (quarterly) adjustments and enforcement of tariffs adjustments based on macroeconomic factors with a path towards cost reflectivity
comment: NERC issues MYTO tariff orders for each distribution company on a monthly basis, exceeding the quarterly adjustment commitment; the September 2026 orders (Nos. 088–098) were issued on 2 September 2026 and cover all eleven DisCos. The MYTO methodology incorporates macroeconomic indices outside licensee control, including inflation, the NGN/USD exchange rate, gas prices, available generation capacity and the transmission loss factor. Progress towards cost reflectivity remains partial: Band A tariffs, exceeding ₦200/kWh, are close to cost-reflective levels, while other bands continue to require subsidy support amid FX volatility, rising gas costs and collection constraints.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: Put in place a subsidy scheme that provides a universal and flat limited subsidy to each connected customer
comment: Work is ongoing, in coordination with NERC and the Special Adviser on Oil and Gas, to develop a framework for the Power Consumer Assistance Fund (PCAF) as part of the broader sector debt-reduction and transition-to-cost-reflective-tariffs study. World Bank household survey and NLSS data on income and electricity expenditure will support the design of a targeted subsidy mechanism for economically vulnerable consumers. Further government-level decisions and implementation may occur after the national elections, while preparatory technical and institutional work continues.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery

Both the tariff review and the operatioanlisation of PCAF will be implemented under the existing subsidy management (i.e., MRO)

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: Approval of the Power Sector Debt resolution scheme for GENCOs and Discos on arrears owed by FG as a line item in the 2025 budget.
comment: Under the ₦4 trillion Multi-Instrument Issuance Programme approved by the Federal Executive Council, the Series 1 bond opened in December 2025 and closed at ₦501 billion, comprising ₦300 billion (60%) raised from the capital markets and ₦201 billion (40%) allotted directly to participating generation companies and their gas suppliers. The issuance was fully subscribed and has since been listed on the Nigerian Exchange and FMDQ Securities Exchange. Its first coupon and principal repayment of approximately ₦63.5 billion was met in full and on schedule on 14 July 2026, settling verified obligations to participating GenCos and covering an estimated 22% of settlement obligations under executed agreements; separately, ₦333 billion has been paid to eight participating GenCos, covering 17 power plants. A Series 2 issuance of approximately ₦729 billion was launched in July 2026 to extend settlement to a wider set of generation companies, gas suppliers and service providers, though a public breakdown of its capital-market versus direct-allotment split has not yet been disclosed. Together, Series 1 and Series 2 bring total issuance to approximately ₦1.23 trillion about 31% of the overall ₦4 trillion programme target.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: NERC approves updated Metering Code
comment: NERC has issued the Metering Code for the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry, 3rd Edition, dated March 2026 and published in April 2026, replacing the 2014 edition. The revision was developed by the Metering Code Review Panel following stakeholder consultation and aligns the framework with the Electricity Act 2023.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: FGN through SGDL approves in 2024 a Metering Plan to close the metering gap in the period 2025 to 2027
comment: As at 26 August 2026, 1.3 million smart meters had been delivered under Phase 1 of the Distribution Sector Recovery Programme, of which 668,000 had been installed (65%), leaving about 365,000 awaiting deployment. Roughly 60 per cent of active customers are now metered. NERC's Q1 2026 report recorded 129,224 DISREP installations, up 29.81% on Q4 2025 and bringing cumulative framework installations to 217,784 as at 31 March 2026. Procurement of a further 1.55 million meters under ICB2 has been suspended since 30 April 2026 following an injunction by the Association of Meter Manufacturers of Nigeria over the exclusion of domestic producers.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery

comment: Contract negotiations were suspended pending clarification of pricing structures and cost drivers. MIS deployment is incomplete and fragmented, and the Committee is pushing for harmonisation, transparency in pricing, and future-proof systems capable of integrating meters from multiple initiatives.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: Ensuring implementation of DISCO’s (PIPs) and hold them responsible for them
comment: No strategy or roadmap for distressed DisCos has been approved. Action to date has been case-specific: in August 2026 NERC dissolved the Board of Kaduna Electricity Distribution Plc under sections 75–79 of the Electricity Act over severe insolvency and ₦118.6 billion in additional market debt, appointing an Interim Board with a twelve-month turnaround mandate.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: Provide seed financing for PIP to enable DISCOs to access commercial financing later
comment: Seed financing for DisCo Performance Improvement Plans is provided under the DISREP, on concessional terms structured as Investment Project Financing and Programme-for-Results. The facility finances key PIP components. All DisCos have executed the Shareholders' Loan Agreement and submitted Board Resolutions and Individual Action Plans, except JEDC. The closing date has been extended by 23 months to 30 May 2028, and an additional $308 million is under discussion. Transition to commercial financing remains prospective; no DisCo has raised commercial finance based on DISREP-funded improvements.

commitment: Utilities achieving at least 100 percent operational cost recovery
action: Strengthen regulatory oversight of the distribution companies
comment: NERC has tightened oversight in three ways. First, CapEx Provision Accounts now limit DisCo capital spending to approved Performance Improvement Plan projects. DisCos must obtain a "No Objection" before spending, before awarding contracts, and at each payment milestone. They have asked for the order to be suspended. Second, NERC used its intervention powers at board level in August 2026, dissolving the KAEDC Board. Third, monthly performance factsheets continue to be published. In April 2026, billing efficiency stood at 83.32 per cent and collection efficiency at 80.66 per cent.
